sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of October, 2024  JUDGMENT

The claimant in O.P.(MV)No.916 of 2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Ernakulam is the appellant.

2. The facts in brief are as follows: On 11.12.2017 at 8.30 p.m, while the petitioner was crossing the road at Puthuvyppu Village School Muttam bus stop, the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.KL-7-CH-2867 ridden by the 1 st respondent in the original petition in a rash and negligent manner, hit the claimant - appellant and thereby she fell to the ground and sustained grievous injuries.

Claiming compensation, she approached the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam by OP(MV)No.916/2018.
3.

The Insurance Company entered appearance before the Tribunal and disputed the claim and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the appellant/ claimant and not due to the negligence of the driver of the ..3..
2024:KER:76751 offending vehicle.
On behalf of the claimant, Exts.A1 to A10 were produced.
No oral or documentary evidence was produced on the side of the Insurance Company.
The claimant/appellant claimed that she was earning an income of Rs.10,000/-, but the Tribunal fixed the notional income at Rs.8,000/- and awarded the following compensation:

Aggrieved by the insufficiency in the grant of compensation, the appellant has approached this Court.

4. Heard, Smt.Baby M.M. - learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri.Lal K.Joseph - learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the claimant/appellant was aged 58 years old and working as a Sweeper at the time of the accident.
The accident occurred on 11.12.2017.
She was also admitted as an inpatient for 11 days.

The Tribunal, though took notice of the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant/appellant, which is extracted in paragraph 15 of the Award, did not deem fit to consider the fixation of notional income in terms of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She also further pointed out that the appellant had suffered loss of earning for nearly six months, but the Tribunal granted only three months of loss of earning.

Considering the ..5..
2024:KER:76751 nature of the injuries, the Tribunal ought to have granted reasonable compensation towards the future treatment also.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company pointed out that what is claimed by the appellant in her claim petition is only Rs.10,000/- and therefore, this Court cannot fix the notional income at Rs.11,000/- going by the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra).
He further pointed out that reasonable compensation has been granted by the Tribunal, hence no interference is called for.
7. I have considered the rival submissions raised across the Bar.

sentences.text: It is true that the appellant/claimant had only claimed Rs.10,000/- as income earned by her.

However, the moment the Tribunal has found that there is no evidence to support the claim of fixation of the income, then necessarily the Tribunal has to fall back on the principles of grant of notional income based on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra).
There is no absolute rule that, in a claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Tribunal shall be guided only by the averments contained in the application.

It may be ..6..
2024:KER:76751 true that on the facts of this case, the claimant had claimed only Rs.10,000/- as income, however, going by the principles laid down in Ramachandrappa (supra), when the claimant is entitled to have the notional income fixed at Rs.11,000/-, this Court sees no reason as to why the said relief cannot be granted to the appellant.
Accordingly, the Award of the Tribunal fixing the notional income at Rs.8,000/- to be interfered.
9. Added to the above, the appellant is also entitled to receive enhanced compensation under the non pecuniary heads also, which according to this Court would be reasonable.
In the result, the appeal is allowed.
The notional income of the claimant is fixed at Rs.11,000/-.
The enhanced compensation for which the appellant is entitled is as follows:

Heads Amount Total Enhanced  awarded by the compensation amount of  Tribunal awarded compensation Loss of earnings 24,000 66,000 42,000  (11,000x6) (66,000-24,000)
Expenses for extra 2,000/- 5,000/- 3,000/-

nourishment Compensation for 50,000 60,000 10,000 Pain and (60,000-50,000)
sufferings

Compensation for nil 25,000 25,000 future treatment Total enhanced amount of compensation Rs.80,000/-
 ..7..
 2024:KER:76751

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of Rs.80,000/- (Rupees eighty thousand only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization together with proportionate costs.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
The claimant shall furnish the details of the bank account to the Insurance Company for transfer of the amount.

4 appellant will not be entitled to interest for a period of 367 days, which represents the period of delay in filing the appeal.
